headline: UN diplomats in Geneva failed to agree on rules regulating autonomous weapons, as Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on AI data centers built outside the US and new reporting detailed Jensen Huang's 'lack of candor' before his ouster.

points.text: UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week failed to agree on rules regulating autonomous weapons, or so-called 'killer robots.'
President Trump said he would block US companies from building data centers overseas or impose a 'tremendous tax' on them if they do, as part of a push to keep AI infrastructure in the country.
Wired reported that Nvidia's board was most alarmed by former CEO Jensen Huang's 'lack of candor,' rather than the affairs themselves, ahead of his resignation.
A new METR report updated AI's capability trajectory, finding some capabilities still improving exponentially while models lag on tasks requiring other skills.
Wired warned that internet outages are just getting started, as AI forces companies to patch systems faster while attackers race to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities.
